The clinical picture of severe respiratory distress with grunting and retractions, combined with a chest X-ray showing a ground-glass appearance and mediastinal shift (often mimicking ground glass due to bowel in the chest), is highly suggestive of a congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The "normal readings" in previous tests likely reflect technical errors or misinterpretations in this context. I suspect the lung fields are actually compressed by abdominal viscera rather than showing primary parenchymal disease. I will request immediate images to confirm the presence of bowel loops in the thoracic cavity and rule out other causes like TTN or severe PPHN.
